To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ASE of the uplink of dense SCNs with LoS and non-LoS transmissions can be significantly enhanced by a small UL power compensation factor, which is contrary to previous works that do no distinguish LoS and non-line-of sight (NLoS).

the ASE of the uplink of dense SCNs with LoS and/or NLoS transmissions is significantly impacted by the UL power compensation factor and UE density, which is in contrast to the previous works that do predict that a larger UL compensation factor always leads to a higher ASE in the UL.

the UL ASE in a dense SCN can be greatly improved by increasing the UL power compensation factor, while the UL ASE in sparse SCNs is not affected by the UL power compensation; the ASE of the dense SCN is dominated by the LoS transmissions, while the ASE of sparse SCNs is dominated by the NLoS transmissions; the UL ASE of the dense SCNs can be greatly improved if the UE density is larger than 102 UEs/km 2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of LoS transmissions in the uplink of dense SCNs.
the impact of LoS/NLoS transmissions in dense SCNs, which can be considered a first step towards the design of future dense SCNs.
the impact of LoS transmission in the UL of SCNs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ASE in the uplink of dense SCNs can be maximized by a smaller UL power control factor, while a larger one would be more appropriate in the uplink for sparse SCNs.
the UL power compensation factor should be carefully selected to maximize the ASE of dense SCNs.
the optimal power compensation factor for the UL in the dense SCNs is smaller than that for sparse SCNs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ASE in the uplink of dense SCNs can be greatly improved by considering LoS and NLos transmissions.

the UL power compensation factor should be chosen according to the UE density in dense SCNs, and a smaller UL power compensating factor is more suitable than a larger one in the range of 102~103Ues/km2.
, for a dense SCN, a smaller UL power compensations factor is preferred for a higher ASE, and a larger UL power compensations is preferred for a larger coverage probability.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ASE of dense SCNs can be significantly enhanced by properly designing the UL power compensation factor and by differentiating the LoS and NLos transmissions.
a larger UL compensation factor should be used in dense SCNs, while a smaller UL power compensating factor should be used for sparse SCNs.
the ASE of the uplink in dense SCNs can be greatly improved by considering LoS and NloS transmissions, and by properly adjusting the UL power compensation factor.
